summary: Yiu Wing Chan is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong by 2013, studying under doctoral supervisor K. L. Dhammajoti.

Yoel Hoffmann (1937–2023) was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Hanazono, Tel Aviv under Ben-Ami Scharfstein, and Kyoto University (PhD ~1977), later serving as professor at the University of Haifa (~1983–2003).

Yohei Kawajiri is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He was a research associate at Chikushi Jogakuen University (attested 2008–2013, 2022) and a special researcher at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 2011).

Yoichi Fukuda (born 1954) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts as a full-time researcher at Toyo Bunko (attested 1986–1991) and as a professor at Otani University (attested 2003, 2015).
Yoichi Kawada (born 1937) is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies who served as Director of The Institute of Oriental Philosophy (attested 2002, 2016).
Yong Hua is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College (attested 2014) under supervisors Tilak Kariyawasam and Fa Qing.

Yongdzin Tenzin Namdak (born 1926) is a Tibetology and religious studies scholar. Educated at Tengchen, Yungdrung Ling, and Menri Monastery (Geshe 1953), he taught at Menri, founded Triten Norbutse Monastery, and held visiting posts at SOAS (1961) and Munich (1969).

Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche (born 1975) works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Palpung Sherabling Monastery and Dzongsar Institute under teachers including Nyoshul Khenpo and Khenchen Kunga Wangchuk, becoming abbot of Palpung Sherabling around 1994.
Yongshan He specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at McMaster University under James A. Benn, Shayne Clarke, and Mark Rowe.

Yongtong Tang (1893–1964) was a Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology scholar. He studied at Tsinghua and Harvard under Charles Rockwell Lanman and Irving Babbitt, later holding posts at Southeast University, National Southwestern Associated University, and Peking University.

Yonten Gyatso (1933–2002) was a Tibetology and history scholar. He earned a Geshé degree at Drepung Gomang Dratsang and a diploma at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, where he served as research advisor for Tibetan Studies.

Yoshifumi Honjo (born 1951) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at Kyoto University under Hajime Sakurabe, he held academic positions at Kyoto University, Kobe Women's University, Otani University, and Bukkyo University.

Yoshifumi Mizuno (born 1958) is an Indology and linguistics scholar. Educated at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies and the University of Tokyo, he held posts at the University of Tokyo and served as associate professor at TUFS (2000–2024).

Yoshihide Yoshizu (1943–2014) specialized in Buddhist studies and sinology. He completed his doctoral studies at Komazawa University under Shigeo Kamata and Shoson Miyamoto, later serving there as lecturer (1971) and professor (2001).

Yoshihiko Amino (1929–2004) was a Japanese history and Japanology scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1947–1950) and held academic posts at Nagoya University (~1973–1980) and Kanagawa University (~1980–1995).
Yoshihiko Nasu works in Buddhist studies. He served as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 2007) and held leadership positions at Kongoju and Kongojushinkai (attested 2017).

Yoshihiko Sakurai is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (attested 2001). He served there as a part-time lecturer (attested 2003) and as a researcher at the Jodo Shinshu Hongwanji-ha Research Center.
Yoshihiro Matsunami (born 1945) is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who served as a professor (attested 1991–1999) and later president (2001) of Taisho University.

Yoshihito Muroji is a Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology scholar. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen and held posts at Koyasan University, Kyoto University, and Shiga University of Medical Science.
Yoshiko Shimabukuro (born 1911) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied at Kyoto Chuo Bukkyo Gakuen (-1936) and Kyoto Women's University (1936–1940).
